name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,689

clue.text: Famous figure playing games with sailor

indicators.note: children playing move about freely, so the letters here are rearranged at will

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A celebrity is spotted playing games alongside a sailor, perhaps on a cruise ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing games' reads as one activity, but 'playing' is the signal to shuffle the next word. Tar is the crossword's favourite sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge celebrity is a very well-known person, someone everybody recognises, which is what a famous figure means.

clue.text: Second line written in pen predominantly

indicators.note: words written in something sit inside it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, as in 'wait a mo'
L is the standard abbreviation for line
a pig's pen is a sty

explanation.surface: Someone notes that the second line was written mostly in pen rather than pencil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' is a short spell of time, as in 'just a second', not a position in a list; 'pen' is an animal enclosure rather than a writing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something that holds for the greater part, true for the most part though not entirely.

clue.text: Happy to welcome easy-going host

indicators.note: to welcome a guest is to take them in, so one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: the older sense of gay, cheerful
lax means relaxed, not strict

explanation.surface: A cheerful guest is delighted to be greeted by a relaxed, informal host.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' looks like the person throwing the party, but it is the definition in its sense of a great crowd: GA(LAX)Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A host can mean a vast number, as in a heavenly host, and a galaxy is likewise a brilliant assembly of many stars or people.

clue.text: Somewhat dreary task upset lecherous fellow

indicators.note: somewhat means only to some extent, so just part of the following words is taken
something upset is knocked over, and in a down clue that turns the letters upside down

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A tedious job annoys a lecherous man, a picture of a lazy lout grumbling at chores.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the letters straddling 'dreary task' from the bottom up. In myth a satyr is a goat-legged woodland spirit known for its lust.
explanation.definitionFit: From the lusty goat-men of Greek myth, the word came to mean any man given to excessive sexual desire, a lecher.

clue.text: Gaslight a politician supporting Catholic in Alabama

definitions.note: loose: an arc lamp is electric, but both are kinds of lamp

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so these letters are enclosed
in a down clue a support sits underneath, so this piece goes below what it holds up

blocks.note: AL is the postal abbreviation for Alabama
RC stands for Roman Catholic
taken as written
a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A political story: a politician backing a Catholic in Alabama is accused of gaslighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gaslight' tempts as the modern verb for psychological manipulation, but it is a noun for a lamp. In a down clue the politician 'supporting' sits underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are artificial light sources of the same era, one burning gas and the other making light with an electric spark between electrodes.

clue.text: Prime explosives and mine cavity

blocks.note: to prime a bomb is to arm it, ready to go off
a coal mine is a pit

explanation.surface: Instructions for blasting: get the explosives ready and dig out a hollow in the mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime explosives' reads as a noun phrase but it is an instruction meaning ARM, and 'cavity' is the body's hollow, not a hole in a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: The armpit is the hollow under the join of arm and shoulder, a small natural hollow in the body.

clue.text: Joy's crushed by Romeo having intercourse

indicators.note: something crushed by another is pressed hard against it, so the two pieces sit side by side

blocks.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
joy is elation, and the 's is kept as a letter

explanation.surface: A romantic tragedy: someone's happiness is shattered by a lover who is sleeping with somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo suggests Shakespeare's lover, but here he is just the letter R, placed in front of ELATION'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Intercourse in its broad sense means dealings between people, and relations are exactly those dealings or connections, sexual or otherwise.

clue.text: Meat suppliers receiving telegram about headgear

indicators.note: to receive something is to take it in, so one piece holds another
turned about means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: pigs supply pork, bacon and ham
a wire is an old word for a telegram

explanation.surface: Butchers receive a telegram concerning hats, an odd business message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meat suppliers' suggests butchers, but it means the animals that the meat comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Periwigs were the long powdered wigs of the 17th and 18th centuries, worn on the head and so a kind of headgear.

clue.text: Model discovered fate in place of worship

indicators.note: dis-covered means with its covers stripped off, so only the inner letters remain
one thing in another sits inside it, so these letters are enclosed

blocks.note: a temple is a building for worship
the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A fashion model learns what destiny holds while visiting a church or shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' means found out in the surface, but split as dis-covered it strips the outer letters off 'fate'.
explanation.definitionFit: A template is a pattern to copy from, and a model can mean exactly that: an example to follow.

clue.text: Drunk embracing heartless lass rocks biannual event

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle has been removed, leaving just the ends
to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
taken as written before its middle goes
drinks served on the rocks come with ice

explanation.surface: A drunk hugs a cruel girl who rocks a festival held twice a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocks' looks like a verb but means the frozen cubes in a drink served on the rocks; 'heartless' leaves only the outer letters of the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The solstices fall twice each year, in June and December, when the sun reaches its furthest point north or south.

clue.text: A revolutionary painting is call to arms

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so these letters face the other way

blocks.note: taken as written
a mural is a painting on a wall

explanation.surface: A rebel's painting acts as a rallying cry, art as propaganda for the revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary painting' sounds like a political artwork, but it is a mural turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarum is the archaic form of alarm, a warning signal summoning soldiers to take up weapons, as in Shakespeare's stage directions.

clue.text: Gag son aboard plane

indicators.note: a passenger aboard a craft is inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
a jet is a type of plane

explanation.surface: A boy on a flight is gagged, perhaps to keep the cabin quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gag' looks like a verb meaning silence, but it is the noun for a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A gag is a comedian's joke, and a jest is likewise something said for amusement, a joke.

clue.text: 10p, say, essentially deducted after large university revel

indicators.note: the essence is the very centre, and deducting it takes away the middle letter
following on means coming later in the line, so the earlier pieces lead

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
U is the abbreviation for university
X is ten in Roman numerals
p is said as pee, which is to urinate

explanation.surface: A student's spending money: ten pence taken off after a big university night out.
explanation.walkthrough: '10p' looks like a coin, but it splits into X for ten and P, said as pee. URINATE loses its central N, and the whole follows L and U.
explanation.definitionFit: To luxuriate is to take great pleasure in something, wallowing in comfort, which is what reveling in something means.

clue.text: It may be thrown in dryer

definitions.text: It may be thrown in dryer

blocks.clueFragment: It may be thrown in dryer
blocks.note: surface reading: an item of laundry tossed into a tumble dryer
setter's reading: the idiom for giving up, throwing it in, and the thing is itself something that dries you

explanation.walkthrough: You throw in the towel to concede defeat, and a towel is literally a dryer, so 'dryer' is the item itself rather than the machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A towel is the cloth you dry yourself with, and boxing seconds throw one into the ring to surrender.

clue.text: Extremely meaningful covers of dance record

indicators.note: the covers of a book are its outside, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Cover versions of a dance track turn out to be surprisingly profound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covers' suggests cover versions of songs, but here it means the outside letters of 'dance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep thoughts are profound ones, full of significance, so the word describes something very meaningful.

clue.text: Oscar popped in to unveil outlandish theory

indicators.note: something popped in is slipped inside, so one piece goes into another
outlandish means bizarre and strange, so the letters take on a strange new order

blocks.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: Oscar dropped by to reveal his strange new theory.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes into 'to unveil' and the nine letters are then rearranged. 'Oscar' suggests Wilde or the film award, but is just the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Darwin's theory of evolution, explaining how species change over generations, is the best-known scientific theory of all.

clue.text: Believed ruffian about hotel bar

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: a tough is a violent thug
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a T-bar is a bar shaped like the letter, so the letter stands for it

explanation.surface: A thug is believed to have been hanging around the hotel bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hotel bar' reads as one place, but the hotel goes inside TOUGH and the bar is just a T on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are past forms of verbs for holding an opinion, so 'I thought so' and 'I believed so' mean the same.

clue.text: Innocent prince endlessly entertaining queen on ship

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off
a host entertaining a guest has them inside the house, so one piece holds another
in a down clue one thing on another sits above it, so this piece comes first

blocks.note: Hamlet is Shakespeare's Prince of Denmark
R is short for regina, Latin for queen
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A blameless prince plays host to the queen for ever aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The prince is Shakespeare's Dane, cut short; in a down clue 'on' puts him above the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Something harmless does no damage and means no wrong, just as an innocent person or remark is free of malice.

clue.text: Teacher read out moving letters about Charlie

indicators.note: letters that move change places, so they are rearranged
about means around, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: taken as written
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A teacher reads aloud some touching letters about a pupil called Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving letters' sounds like emotional correspondence; it means the letters of 'read out' move, with C among them.
explanation.definitionFit: An educator is a person whose job is to instruct others, which is just what a teacher does in school.

clue.text: Article physician regularly copied is like a robot?

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article
Dr is the title of a doctor
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A doctor's article, copied over and over, is accused of being mechanical, like a robot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly copied' suggests plagiarism, but it takes every second letter of 'copied'.
explanation.definitionFit: An android is a robot built in human form; the question mark flags that the word is more usually a noun than an adjective.

clue.text: Study base of object for superficial damage

indicators.note: the base is the bottom, and in a down clue that is the final letter

blocks.note: a den is a private room for work, a study
the final letter

explanation.surface: An insurer inspects the bottom of an item for surface scratches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' looks like a verb meaning examine, but it is the room.
explanation.definitionFit: A dent is a shallow hollow knocked into a surface, a minor bit of damage that does not go deep.

clue.text: Louche airmen abandoned swimmer

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: raffish means disreputable in a rakish way
the Royal Air Force, Britain's air arm

explanation.surface: Disreputable aviators desert a swimmer, leaving him stranded in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAF, Britain's air force, is taken away from the start of RAFFISH.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish is the archetypal swimming creature, so swimmer works as a definition by example.

clue.text: Sporting association covers second pitch? Cunning move!

indicators.note: in a down clue a cover lies on top, so this piece sits above the rest

blocks.note: the FA is England's Football Association
S is the abbreviation for second
pitch in music is tone

explanation.surface: The football authority insures a second ground, and someone hails it as a shrewd tactic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' wants to be a sports field next to 'sporting association', but it is a musical pitch. To pull a fast one is to trick someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling a fast one means tricking someone, so the phrase names a crafty, deceitful manoeuvre.

clue.text: Gradually landowning class swaps sides

indicators.note: the two sides are left and right, so one of those letters is exchanged for the other

blocks.note: the gentry were the landed class below the nobility

explanation.surface: Over time, the landed classes change their political allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: In GENTRY the R for right becomes L for left.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle slope rises gradually, so gently can mean little by little, without sudden change.

clue.text: Most of county setter originally described as destitute

indicators.note: most but not all means the last letter is lost
the origin is the beginning, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: Devon is a county in south-west England
the setter refers to themself as I
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter living mostly in the countryside is said to be penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: DEVON loses its last letter, then I and D follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Destitute of something means wholly lacking it, and devoid of carries exactly that sense of complete absence.

clue.text: Mother meets copper outside a popular gambling centre

indicators.note: something outside another surrounds it, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: ma is an informal word for mother
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mother bumps into a policeman outside a well-known casino.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but it is the metal's symbol CU, which goes round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Macau, on China's south coast, earns more from casinos than anywhere else on Earth, so it is a famous betting hub.

clue.text: Spooner's model relative gets microscopic part

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so initial sounds trade places

blocks.note: to model is to pose for an artist or camera
a niece is a family relative
the two words said aloud with their opening sounds traded

explanation.surface: A fashion model's relative is given a tiny role.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first sounds of POSE and NIECE. 'Microscopic' looks like 'tiny' but means belonging to a microscope.
explanation.definitionFit: The nosepiece is the revolving part of a microscope that holds the objective lenses, so it is a component of that instrument.

clue.text: Sealant placed on borders of tapestry

indicators.note: in a down clue one thing on another sits above it, so this piece comes first
the borders are the edges, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: to put is to place
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A conservator applies sealant around the edges of an old wall hanging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Borders' sounds like the edging of the textile, and here it means just its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Putty is a soft paste that hardens, used to seal panes into window frames, so it is a typical sealant.

clue.text: Require shape-shifting alien to hide truth, initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is kept
hiding something keeps it inside, so one piece goes within another
a shape-shifter changes form, so these letters take a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A science-fiction plot: a shape-changing creature must conceal what is really going on.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside ALIEN and the six letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: If one thing entails another it makes it necessary, so the verb means to require or involve as a consequence.

clue.text: Newspaper defends Tory struggling with old age?

indicators.note: a defender stands round what it protects, so one piece encloses another
something struggling is thrashing about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the FT is the Financial Times
taken as written
W is the abbreviation for with
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A newspaper stands up for a Conservative politician who is finding old age hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old age' looks like the definition, but 'old' supplies O and only 'age?' defines, the question mark showing it is one example of an age.
explanation.definitionFit: A person can be that many years old, so the number is an example of an age, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Psychiatrist's contract

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for a psychiatrist, from headshrinker
second meaning: to become smaller

explanation.walkthrough: The 's makes it read as a therapist's legal agreement, but it stands for 'is', joining two meanings; 'contract' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal slang for a mental-health doctor, and as a verb it means to get smaller or draw in.

clue.text: Tearful daughters crossing river in middle of storm

indicators.note: to cross something is to stretch across it, so one piece spans another
one thing in another sits inside it, so these letters are enclosed

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter, doubled for the plural
the eye of a storm is its calm centre
the Wye is a river on the England-Wales border

explanation.surface: Weeping daughters ford a river in the middle of a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: The river goes inside the calm centre of the storm, and the two daughters wrap round the lot. 'Middle of storm' looks like a letter selection, but it means the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Dewy eyes are moist with tears, so the phrase describes someone sentimental or on the verge of crying.
